div.head: CHn cor 14.1
div.ab: Et si quis inde aliquid retinuerit, ille super quem inuentum fuerit grauiter michi emendabit.
Et si quis inde aliquid retinuerit, ille super quem inventum fuerit graviter mihi emendabit.
But if anyone shall thereafter retain anything, he in whose possession it is found shall pay heavy compensation to me.
div.note: Added October 2026 from Robertson pp. 282–283 (text and translation); Liebermann’s text added from Gesetze I p. 522, October 2026 (two independent readings of the page images)

note.seg: Presentis uero ecclesie monachis libertates, dignitates regiasque consuetudines sibi per cartas regum olim confirmatas concedo interpolirt Westm. Lond. Cust.
Presentis uero ecclesie monachis libertates, dignitates regiasque consuetudines sibi per cartas regum olim confirmatas concedo interpolated in Westm. Lond. Cust.

Die Fälschung{55}, auch in Rs, benutzt den Freibrief von 1136, oder dieser hielt sich an den Westminsterschen Text. Die Zeile trägt lokal partikularen Charakter, im Ggs. zum allgemein Englischen des Freibriefs; sie hätte, wenn authentisch, Ort, Heiligen oder Oberhaupt der Kirche und die königlichen Erteiler oder den Inhalt der Privilegien genannt. Sie meint Westminster laut Test{6}. Dass man im 12. Jh. in Westminster Urkunden fälschte, ergibt Robinson Gilbert Crispin Index: forgeries. Vgl. o. Einl. 13

The forgery{55}, found in Rs too, uses the charter of liberties of 1136, or else the latter followed the Westminster text. The line is of a local, particular character, in contrast to the general English character of the charter of liberties; had it been authentic, it would have named the place, the saint or the head of the church, and the royal grantors or the content of the privileges. It means Westminster, according to Test{6}. That charters were forged at Westminster in the 12th cent. is shown by Robinson Gilbert Crispin Index: forgeries. Cf. above Introduction 13
